nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Ni foam (NF) with suitable size (2×2 cm) was carefully cleaned with HCl (≈37 wt%) in an ultrasound bath for 5 min to remove the oxide layer on the surface, and then cleaned via ultrapure water and ethanol for 3 times.

nodes.name: Ni(Fe)O hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (3 mmol) and FeCl3·6H2O (0.2 mmol) were dissolved in a mixed solution of ultrapure water (25 mL) and methanol (15 mL) under stirring for 30 min. The obtained solution with a piece of cleaned NF were transferred into a 50 mL autoclave and maintained at 120°C for 8 h. The as-deposited NF was washed with ultrapure water and alcohol and dried at 60°C, and then heated at 350°C for 2 h in air to obtain the Fe doped NiO sample (named as Ni(Fe)O). 0.2 mmol Fe doping content was selected for the subsequent synthesis due to its best activity (see Fig. S1).

nodes.name: Ni(Fe)O to Ni(Fe)OOH conversion
nodes.procedure: The Ni(Fe)O (1×1 cm) sample was employed as working electrode to conduct cyclic voltammetry (CV) activation for 60 cycles at a rate of 50 mV s⁻¹ (see Fig. S2). The obtained sample was further treated by OER operation and directly named as Ni(Fe)OOH.

nodes.name: Au NPs electrodeposition on Ni(Fe)OOH
nodes.procedure: A standard three-electrode system was employed, where Ni(Fe)OOH (1×1 cm) was directly used as working electrode. 20 μL of 0.04 M HAuCl4·4H2O solution was added to 80 mL of NaCl solution (0.05 M), which was stirred for 0.5 h to obtain the homogeneous mixture as an electrolyte. The content of HAuCl4·4H2O was optimized and a content of 20 μL was found to be optimal (see Fig.S3). The electrochemical deposition process was implemented by CV for 20 cycles with a voltage range from -0.2 to -0.6 V vs. SCE (saturated calomel electrode (SCE)) at a scan rate of 80 mV s⁻¹. The obtained sample was further treated by OER operation and the samples after OER were directly named as Au@Ni(Fe)OOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines Au loading of 35.15 wt% in Au@Ni(Fe)OOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The amount of supported Au in Au@Ni(Fe)OOH was about 35.15 wt%, which was determined by the different concentration of Au ion in electrolyte before and after electro-deposition.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ FTIR of Ni(Fe)O at 1.60 V vs RHE shows Ni-O vibrations at 645.71, 663.59 cm⁻¹, -OH bending at 534.84 cm⁻¹, and new NiOOH stretching peak at 543.31 cm⁻¹ appearing with activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The infrared peaks centered at 645.71 and 663.59 cm⁻¹ are assigned to the distinctive vibration of Ni-O and the peak at 534.84 cm⁻¹ is attributed to the bending vibration of -OH. Notably, a new peak at 543.31 cm⁻¹ gradually appears as the electrochemical activation proceeded.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum of Ni(Fe)O shows peak at 503 cm⁻¹ that disappears after activation, with new peak at 558 cm⁻¹ characteristic of NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, the Raman spectrum of Ni(Fe)O shows a remarkable peak at 503 cm⁻¹. In contrast, the peak disappears, while a new peak emerges at 558 cm⁻¹ after electrochemical activation.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of all samples exhibit only pure phase of NiO, with no characteristic peaks from oxyhydroxides or Au NPs detected due to low crystallinity and low Au content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It turns out that all patterns of the involved samples exhibit only a pure phase of NiO (see Fig. S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Fe)OOH shows vertically arranged nanosheets forming porous morphology with larger inter-sheet spacing; Au@Ni(Fe)OOH shows no significant morphological variation after Au decoration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was performed to explore the morphological and micro-structural variation upon Au NPs decoration as well as Fe doping, as shown in Fig. S8, Fig. 2a and 2 g.
